11.1d — Create PT: Build Day 3

The list works (11.1b), the algorithm works (11.1c). Today: the parts the VIDEO shows — input the user gives, output the user sees, and the 60-second path through your program that will become the recording. Build day for the audience.

Build Day ~50 min

Input (the rubric row: a program that responds):

  • Keyboard, mouse, buttons, or a text field — your choice, but it must be GENUINE input: the user's action changes program behavior (1.4 was your first one; a PT grader needs to SEE it change the output)
  • Two inputs beat one: a "draw card" AND a "sort hand" proves the program's responsiveness twice

Output (what the video shows as behavior):

  • Upgrade your Day-1 Debug.Logs into on-screen text or UI — the video is graded on OBSERVABLE behavior
  • The output should DIFFER with different input — that is the whole point of input/output as a pair: type one thing, see result A; type another, see result B. Film both.

The demo path (design it like a level — 7.5 skills!):

  1. Seconds 0–10: state the purpose in text on screen (not voiceover-only)
  2. 10–35: give one input, show the algorithm's result (list visibly changes)
  3. 35–55: give a different input, show the different output
  4. 55–60: the list's final state, readable on screen

Rehearse it three times TODAY — the recording happens on 11.2a and takes under 5 minutes if the path is tight, or an hour of retakes if it is not.

Bug Hunt: Video-day disasters

  1. Your demo needs the CONSOLE open to show behavior. Why is console-only output a rubric problem (the grader watches a video — what software will they NOT have)?
  2. The input works but a typo dead-ends the program mid-demo. What was Day 3's missing ritual (10.1e freeze + build — but for a PT video)?
  3. You realize the algorithm output takes 30 seconds of watching nothing. The video has a 1-minute cap — what do you cut (not the input; not the output; the WAITING)?
Close of Day ~5 min

Tinker: Dress rehearsal

  1. Run the demo path end to end, out loud, with a classmate as your camera. Fix what breaks.
  2. Commit + push: "11.1d: input/output + demo path".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Demonstrate input changing program behavior on screen
  • Show output that differs per input
  • Walk the 60-second demo path without console output
  • Rehearse it in front of a witness and survive
